findings.text: non-blocking: `_canonical_test_ids`, `_after_suite_arm` and `_after_suite_added_guard` duplicate the manifest suite-arm capability `promotion_checks._head_suite_failure_ids` (reckon/crew/promotion_checks.py:1995) and `_baseline_suite_failure_ids` (reckon/crew/promotion_checks.py:1955) already own in a module this file already imports, so the rule for reading a failure-id set now has two implementations that can diverge, and the peer section that consolidates failure comparison will have to reconcile this copy.

non-blocking: `_undisposed_finding_guard` enumerates through `findings._record_findings`, which for a code review returns the record's findings list unfiltered (reckon/crew/findings.py:170), while `record_finding_disposition` enumerates through `repair.review_findings`, which skips an entry stating no claim (reckon/crew/repair.py:133); a claimless finding ahead of a disposed one shifts the index, so the guard reads `open` for a finding index the disposition writer refuses to accept findings for.

blocking: On a landing the pass calls `record_landed_exemptions`, whose `_excusable_finding_indexes` (reckon/crew/recovery_review_acceptance.py:65) returns every non-blocking finding regardless of any existing disposition, and `record_finding_disposition` overwrites the entry (reckon/crew/review_dispositions.py:497); because this change makes a disposition mandatory before landing, the `folded:<node>` a coordinator records is rewritten to `exempted:<reason>` on the very next pass and the node it names is lost.

non-blocking: The diff reverses three assertions in a file outside every declared write path, superseding the landed contract that a review's non-blocking findings do not hold the landing; the reversal is disclosed in the fragment and required by the done_when, but it changes another section's accepted behaviour without that section's coordinator.
